- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows strong upward bias, reduce forecast peak by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (prices trending down from recent highs), model should not overreact to short-term sentiment spikes.  
- Forecast should not lag by more than 1–2 days relative to sentiment turning points — especially if sentiment shifts sharply.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement at 1–2% above recent low to avoid false optimism.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent trend, not sentiment alone.  
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (especially >0.8) should be corrected by reducing forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days unless confirmed by new data.
